answer: Optical physical unclonable functions curb Sybil attacks by tethering agent identities to unique scattering tokens. To authenticate, an agent refracts a violet laser challenge through an internal prism to produce a deterministic speckle response. An attacker incurs the verifiable fabrication cost of distinct microstructures per identity, creating an economic canyon that software emulators cannot cross. However, ambient temperature shifts can alter speckle patterns, causing false rejections.
